Despite recent advances in vision\u2013language models (VLMs), their use in healthcare remains limited by a lack of interpretability and a tendency to produce direct, unexplainable outputs. This opacity undermines their reliability in medical settings, where transparency and justification are critically important. To address this limitation, we propose a zero-shot chain-of-thought prompting framework that guides VLMs to perform multi-step reasoning before arriving at an answer. By encouraging the model to break down the problem, analyze both visual and contextual cues, and construct a stepwise explanation, the approach makes the reasoning process explicit and clinically meaningful. We evaluate the framework on the PMC-VQA benchmark, which includes authentic radiological images and expert-level prompts. In a comparative analysis of three leading VLMs, Gemini 2.5 Pro achieved the highest accuracy (72.48%), followed by Claude 3.5 Sonnet (69.00%) and GPT-4o Mini (67.33%). The results demonstrate that chain-of-thought prompting significantly improves both reasoning transparency and performance in MedVQA tasks.<\/jats:p>","DOI":"10.3390\/math13142322","type":"journal-article","is-referenced-by-count":7,"title":["Analyzing Diagnostic Reasoning of Vision\u2013Language Models via Zero-Shot Chain-of-Thought Prompting in Medical Visual Question Answering"],"author":[{"ORCID":"https:\/\/orcid.org\/0009-0005-1684-8211","authenticated-orcid":false,"given":"Fatema Tuj Johora","family":"Faria","sequence":"first","affiliation":[{"name":"Department of Computer Science and Engineering, Ahsanullah University of Science and Technology, Dhaka 1208, Bangladesh"}],"role":[{"vocabulary":"crossref","role":"author"}]},{"ORCID":"https:\/\/orcid.org\/0000-0002-0029-0859","authenticated-orcid":false,"given":"Laith H.","family":"Baniata","sequence":"additional","affiliation":[{"name":"School of Computing, Gachon University, Seongnam 13120, Republic of Korea"}],"role":[{"vocabulary":"crossref","role":"author"}]},{"ORCID":"https:\/\/orcid.org\/0000-0001-7676-9869","authenticated-orcid":false,"given":"Ahyoung","family":"Choi","sequence":"additional","affiliation":[{"name":"School of Computing, Gachon University, Seongnam 13120, Republic of Korea"}],"role":[{"vocabulary":"crossref","role":"author"}]},{"ORCID":"https:\/\/orcid.org\/0000-0002-0281-1726","authenticated-orcid":false,"given":"Sangwoo","family":"Kang","sequence":"additional","affiliation":[{"name":"School of Computing, Gachon University, Seongnam 13120, Republic of Korea"}],"role":[{"vocabulary":"crossref","role":"author"}]}],"container-title":["Mathematics"],"issued":{"date-parts":[[2025,7,21]]},"URL":"https:\/\/doi.org\/10.3390\/math13142322"},{"abstract":"<jats:p><strong> Introduction <\/strong> Large language models (LLMs) like ChatGPT have transformed how we use artificial intelligence, excelling at tasks like writing essays, answering questions, and even holding conversations. Current baseline prompting methods, such as Chain-of-Thought (CoT), Program-of-Thought (PoT), Chain-of-Code (CoC), and Contrastive CoT (CCoT), often yield fragmented results that lack the structural integrity needed for safety-critical IEC 61131-3 synthesis. This paper introduces CoT+ (Chain-of-Thought Extended), a unified prompting architecture that integrates these four paradigms into a deterministic, multi-stage pipeline.The novelty of this research lies in its rigorous three-layer validation framework, utilizing Human-in-the-Loop (HITL), LLM-in-the-Loop (LITL), and Bilingual Evaluation Understudy (BLEU) score analysis. To provide \"double justification\" for the superiority of CoT+, we employ an advanced Inter-Rater Reliability (IRR) assessment using Cohen\u2019s (\u03ba) for pairwise agreement and Krippendorff\u2019s (\u03b1) for multi-rater consistency. This dual-layered statistical approach ensures that performance gains are not only observable across lexical and semantic layers but are also mathematically robust and validator-agnostic. Our results demonstrate that CoT+ achieves significantly higher safety compliance and cross-validator stability than existing baselines. This research contributes: (i) a deployment-oriented prompting template for industrial PLC synthesis, and (ii) a fully reproducible,\u00a0IRR-qualified validation methodology designed for external verification in safety-critical domains.<\/jats:p>","DOI":"10.2139\/ssrn.6247781","type":"posted-content","is-referenced-by-count":0,"title":["CoT+ (Chain-of-Thought Extended): A Reproducible automated software bug detection; however, they lack the global understanding of the given code. Consequently, their performance tends to degrade, especially when they are applied to large interconnected code bases or complex modular programs. Recently, Large Language Models (LLMs) have proven to be effective at capturing dependencies among multiple interconnected modules in the codebase. This motivated us to propose the Flow-Graph-Driven Multi-Agent Framework (FGDM), which is composed of four agents that operate in a sequential manner. The framework converts the received code to a flow graph, identifies the erroneous segments, and further generates the repaired code. All the employed agents utilize Chain-of-Thought (COT) and Tree-of-Thoughts (TOT) prompts. Additionally, we also integrated with the FAISS vector database to retrieve similar previous bugs and their repairs. We demonstrated the efficacy of the proposed framework over 100 programs from several projects, including Ansible, Black, FastAPI, Keras, Luigi, Matplotlib, Pandas, Scrapy, SpaCy, and Tornado in both C and Python programs. Our experiments demonstrate that the FGDM outperforms the extant approaches and yielded reductions with a mean of 24.33 and 8.37 in Levenshtein distance and similarities of 0.951 and 0.974 in cosine
